title: Daskam 42 – Shakatasura-vadha
description: On Krishna’s birth-star day, the cart is shattered; Vraja sees the infant safe, receives the Brahmins’ blessings, and rejoices in his childhood pastimes.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदापि जन्मर्क्षदिने तव प्रभो
निमन्त्रितज्ञातिवधूमहीसुरा ।
महानसस्त्वां सविधे निधाय सा
महानसादौ ववृते व्रजेश्वरी ॥ ४२-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Yashoda, planned to celebrate Krishna's birth star day and invited Brahmins and relatives, friends to her house. She left Krishna in a cloth made as cradle under a cart and got busy in organising feast for guests.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadāpi janmarkṣadine tava prabho
nimantritajñātivadhūmahīsurā |
mahānasastvāṃ savidhe nidhāya sā
mahānasādau vavṛte vrajeśvarī || 42-1 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: Suddenly,  fearful cries and confused voices of various boys who were appointed by Yashoda to protect Krishna, mingled with the sounds of the crackling and breaking sound of wood.
Then hearing the terrific sound, frightened, the Gopikas came running with anxiety. They saw baby Krishna lying amongst the frightful big pieces of broken wood strewn all around.

stanzas.sanskrit:
शिशोरहो किं किमभूदिति द्रुतं
प्रधाव्य नन्दः पशुपाश्च भूसुराः ।
भवन्तमालोक्य यशोदया धृतं
समाश्वसन्नश्रुजलार्द्रलोचनाः ॥ ४२-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Nandagopan, Gopas and the Brahmins rushed to the scene, worried as to what happened to the child and became free of anxiety, after seeing the child safe in Yashoda's hands.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śiśoraho kiṃ kimabhūditi drutaṃ
pradhāvya nandaḥ paśupāśca bhūsurāḥ |
bhavantamālokya yaśodayā dhṛtaṃ
samāśvasannaśrujalārdralocanāḥ || 42-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कस्को नु कौतस्कुत एष विस्मयो
विशङ्कटं यच्छकटं विपाटितम् ।
न कारणं किञ्चिदिहेति ते स्थिताः
स्वनासिकादत्तकरास्त्वदीक्षकाः ॥ ४२-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas awestruck with fingers on their noses, wondered how the cart could have been broken as there was no sign of any one around.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kasko nu kautaskuta eṣa vismayo
viśaṅkaṭaṃ yacchakaṭaṃ vipāṭitam |
na kāraṇaṃ kiñcidiheti te sthitāḥ
svanāsikādattakarāstvadīkṣakāḥ || 42-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कुमारकस्यास्य पयोधरार्थिनः
प्ररोदने लोलपदाम्बुजाहतम् ।
मया मया दृष्टमनो विपर्यगा-
-दितीश ते पालकबालका जगुः ॥ ४२-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The children who were guarding baby Krishna, said that as the child was hungry and crying for milk, baby kicked his lotus legs which hit the cart and broke it.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kumārakasyāsya payodharārthinaḥ
prarodane lolapadāmbujāhatam |
mayā mayā dṛṣṭamano viparyagā-
-ditīśa te pālakabālakā jaguḥ || 42-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भिया तदा किञ्चिदजानतामिदं
कुमारकाणामतिदुर्घटं वचः ।
भवत्प्रभावाविदुरैरितीरितं
मनागिवाशङ्क्यत दृष्टपूतनैः ॥ ४२-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Few Gopas ruled out the statement of boys as baseless. However some Gopas who have earlier seen the incident of Putana's moksham could not reject the statement altogether.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhiyā tadā kiñcidajānatāmidaṃ
kumārakāṇāmatidurghaṭaṃ vacaḥ |
bhavatprabhāvāvidurairitīritaṃ
manāgivāśaṅkyata dṛṣṭapūtanaiḥ || 42-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रवालताम्रं किमिदं पदं क्षतं
सरोजरम्यौ नु करौ विराजितौ ।
इति प्रसर्पत्करुणातरङ्गिता-
स्त्वदङ्गमापस्पृशुरङ्गनाजनाः ॥ ४२-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopikas moved with concern and sympathy, caressed and gently checked for any injury in baby Krishna's tender leaf like legs and lotus flower like hands.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pravālatāmraṃ kimidaṃ padaṃ kṣataṃ
sarojaramyau nu karau virājitau |
iti prasarpatkaruṇātaraṅgitā-
stvadaṅgamāpaspṛśuraṅganājanāḥ || 42-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अये सुतं देहि जगत्पतेः कृपा-
-तरङ्गपातात्परिपातमद्य मे ।
इति स्म सङ्गृह्य पिता त्वदङ्गकं
मुहुर्मुहुः श्लिष्यति जातकण्टकः ॥ ४२-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Nandagopan took the child in his hands from Yashoda and hugged the child again and again, saying repeatedly that the child was protected by Lord Hari in his limitless mercy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aye sutaṃ dehi jagatpateḥ kṛpā-
-taraṅgapātātparipātamadya me |
iti sma saṅgṛhya pitā tvadaṅgakaṃ
muhurmuhuḥ śliṣyati jātakaṇṭakaḥ || 42-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अनोनिलीनः किल हन्तुमागतः
सुरारिरेवं भवता विहिंसितः ।
रजोऽपि नो दृष्टममुष्य तत्कथं
स शुद्धसत्त्वे त्वयि लीनवान् ध्रुवम् ॥ ४२-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Chakatasura, enemy of devas, disguised as a cart, tried to kill Krishna. However Krishna killed the asura. 
But even a trace of his body or evil nature (Rajas) was not seen as the asura came in contact with Bhagwan and hence the asura attained salvation.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
anonilīnaḥ kila hantumāgataḥ
surārirevaṃ bhavatā vihiṃsitaḥ |
rajo’pi no dṛṣṭamamuṣya tatkathaṃ
sa śuddhasattve tvayi līnavān dhruvam || 42-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रपूजितैस्तत्र ततो द्विजातिभि-
-र्विशेषतो लम्भितमङ्गलाशिषः ।
व्रजं निजैर्बाल्यरसैर्विमोहयन्
मरुत्पुराधीश रुजां जहीहि मे ॥ ४२-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
The Braahmins who were invited showered their blessings on baby Krishna. 
Krishna captivated the entire Vrindhavan with his childhood pastimes. 
Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to remove his affliction and protect him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prapūjitais tatra tato dvijātibhi-
-rviśeṣato lambhitamaṅgalāśiṣaḥ |
vrajaṃ nijairbālyarasairvimohayan
marutpurādhīśa rujaṃ jahīhi me || 42-11 ||
